column3: Close to the Hebrew; the article is joined to the name, “Hassenaah” for “the Senaah.”
Close to the Hebrew; the article is dropped from “Hakkoz,” giving “Koz.”
NKJV renders אֲדֹנֵיהֶם (“their masters,” plural) as “their Lord,” capitalized as God; the Hebrew may refer to human overseers.
Close to the Hebrew; “son of the perfumers” is rendered “one of the perfumers,” and וַיַּעַזְבוּ (“they restored, left”) “fortified.”
NKJV reads “Zabbai” (traditional reading) for written זַכַּי, and renders הֶחֱרָה (“zealously”) as “carefully.”
Close to the Hebrew; הַכִּכָּר (“the surrounding region”) is rendered “the plain.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the temple servants” is transliterated “the Nethinim,” and NKJV supplies “made repairs.”
